title: The fibre functor is an equivalence
statement:
Let $Y$ be connected with a geometric point $\bar y\to Y$. Then the
fibre functor induces an equivalence

$$
F_{\bar y}:\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
\pi_1(Y,\bar y)\text{-}\mathbf{Set},
$$

and likewise on $\mathrm{FLC}(Y)$ under the identification of
[thm-galois-lc-etale], where
$\pi_1(Y,\bar y)=\operatorname{Aut}(F_{\bar y})$ carries the profinite
topology of [def-galois-fibre-functor]; here $\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y)$, $\mathrm{FLC}(Y)$ and the fibres are those of [def-galois-categories]. The equivalence is compatible
with finite limits and colimits. It is compatible with base change: for a morphism $f:Y'\to Y$ with $Y'$ connected and a geometric point $\bar y'$ of $Y'$ with $\bar y=f\circ\bar y'$, there is a continuous homomorphism $f_*:\pi_1(Y',\bar y')\to\pi_1(Y,\bar y)$ such that $|(P\times_YY')_{\bar y'}|\cong|P_{\bar y}|$, naturally in $P\in\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y)$, as $\pi_1(Y',\bar y')$-sets, $\pi_1(Y',\bar y')$ acting on the right through $f_*$. If moreover $f$ is finite etale, then $f_*$ is injective and its image is the stabilizer of the point $\bar y'$ of $|Y'_{\bar y}|$, an open subgroup of $\pi_1(Y,\bar y)$ of finite index: base change to $Y'$ corresponds to the passage to this open subgroup.

proof.text: The existing equivalenceContAction of [lem-fet-galois-category] supplies the finite-etale equivalence with continuous finite G-actions. Apply [thm-galois-lc-etale] to obtain the Yoneda equivalence Phi and its fibre comparison beta. Put E = Phi.inverse followed by equivalenceContAction, and let K be the FLC geometric-stalk functor of [def-galois-fibre-functor]. Whiskering beta inverse by Phi.inverse and composing with the counit gives tau from the underlying lifted finite-set functor of E to K. The fully faithful inclusion of finite sets into lifted sets identifies the corresponding automorphism groups. Precomposition by Phi.inverse is fully faithful on functor categories and therefore also identifies automorphism groups; conjugation by tau then gives an algebraic isomorphism gamma from G to Aut(K), starting with the existing toAutMulEquiv of the finite-etale fibre functor. Its component at F sends x to tau_F(g acting on the down-component of tau_F inverse(x)).

source.place: Theorem 0BND (pione-theorem-fundamental-group) (1), proof: 'Part (1) follows from Lemma 0BNB and Proposition 0BN4'

proof.text: For every F and lifted point z, the formula from step 1 gives gamma(g)_F(tau_F(z)) = tau_F(g acting on z), using tau_F inverse(tau_F(z)) = z. Each evaluation coordinate g -> gamma(g)_F(x) is continuous, since it is the given continuous action on the finite-etale fibre at Phi.inverse(F), followed by a map out of a discrete finite set. The two induced-topology universal properties (first pointwise permutations, then their product) prove continuity of gamma for the evaluation topology of [lem-galois-aut-profinite]. Each K(F) is finite because tau_F is a bijection from a lifted finite fibre; the same lemma makes Aut(K) Hausdorff. A continuous equivalence from compact G to Hausdorff Aut(K) has continuous inverse, so gamma is a topological group isomorphism. The unit of Phi supplies Phi.functor followed by E.functor isomorphic to equivalenceContAction. This proves the FLC clause with its required evaluation action.

proof.text: Both equivalenceContAction and E are equivalences. By [lem-galois-equivalence-preserves-limits], their functors preserve all limits and colimits, hence finite limits and finite colimits. Lean obtains the four required preservation instances directly from these equivalences.

source.place: SGA 1 V §7, p. 115: 'Cette equivalence permet donc d'interpreter les operations courantes de limites projectives et limites inductives finies sur des revetements ... en termes des operations analogues dans C(pi)'

proof.text: Bundle fundamentalGroupMap from [lem-galois-pi1-functoriality] with continuous_fundamentalGroupMap into the continuous homomorphism h. For each cover P, lift the component of pullbackFiberIso to an isomorphism of continuous actions: the commutation equation is exactly fundamentalGroupMap_smul, with the two sides reversed. Naturality is the naturality of pullbackFiberIso after forgetting the action. NatIso.ofComponents assembles these isomorphisms. Its underlying maps are definitionally the required components of pullbackFiberIso.

source.place: Theorem 0BND (pione-theorem-fundamental-group) (3) and its proof via Lemma 0BN5 (pione-lemma-functoriality-galois)

proof.text: *Finite etale base change: the open subgroup.* Let moreover $f$ be finite etale. Then $f_*$ is injective by [lem-galois-pi1-finite-etale-injective], and its image is the stabilizer $U$ of $\bar y'\in|Y'_{\bar y}|$, an open subgroup of index $\#|Y'_{\bar y}|$, finite by [def-galois-categories], by [lem-galois-pi1-finite-etale-image-stabilizer]. Hence $f_*$ is a continuous bijection of the compact group $\pi_1(Y',\bar y')$ onto the Hausdorff group $U$, so a homeomorphism (both are profinite by [lem-galois-aut-profinite], for the topologies of [def-galois-fibre-functor]), and by step 4 base change to $Y'$ followed by $F_{\bar y'}$ is $F_{\bar y}$ followed by restriction of the action to $U\cong\pi_1(Y',\bar y')$.
